summary: This short housekeeping document declares RFC 4693 historic and obsoletes it. It was published for information, not as a standards-track specification, so that readers stop treating the older document as current guidance.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4693 created the IETF Operational Notes series as an experiment for documenting some IETF procedures. After the experiment was terminated, RFC 6393 moved its document to Historic status.

questions: how to move an rfc to historic
why was rfc 4693 moved to historic
when did the ions experiment end
subtitle: The IETF Operational Notes experiment ended, so RFC 4693 is moved to Historic.

tldr.problem: RFC 4693 established the IETF Operational Notes series as an experiment, and the IESG later terminated that experiment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6393 obsoletes RFC 4693 and moves it to Historic to reflect the experiment's closure.
tldr.outcome: The memo points readers to the IESG for details about the termination and the future of IONs.

today: RFC 6393 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 4693, moving it to Historic. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6393.

sections.title: Purpose of RFC 6393
sections.content:
RFC 6393 moves RFC 4693 to Historic status and obsoletes it. The memo says this change reflects the closure of the IETF Operational Notes (IONs) experiment.

RFC 6393 is administrative in nature and states that it has no related security issues.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo records that RFC 4693 is no longer current because the experiment it documented ended. It does not define a technical protocol.

sections.title: What the IONs Series Was For
sections.content: RFC 4693 established the IETF Operational Notes series on an experimental basis under RFC 3933. It was intended to discuss IETF procedures for which the RFC publication process was not an appropriate documentation method.
sections.plainLanguage: IONs were intended for documenting IETF procedures that did not fit the RFC publication process. The series began as an experiment.

sections.title: The Experiment's Closure
sections.content:
Under RFC 3933, the IESG decided in March 2008 to terminate the IONs process experiment. RFC 6393 moves RFC 4693 to Historic to reflect that decision.

The memo does not state why the experiment ended. It directs readers to the IESG for details, including the motivation and future of IONs.
sections.plainLanguage: The IESG ended the IONs experiment in March 2008. This RFC records that decision but does not give the reasons.

references.text: Alvestrand, H., "IETF Operational Notes", RFC 4693, October 2006.
Klensin, J. and S. Dawkins, "A Model for IETF Process Experiments", BCP 93, RFC 3933, November 2004.
